label: Expert-centric writing
summary: Expert-centric writing is the pitfall of creating content from your own perspective and level of understanding rather than your audience's. It tends to happen when a writer works on topics they are not an expert on, and compensates by defaulting to an expert frame instead of the audience's frame. Audience modelling is the direct counter to this pattern.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike flags expert-centric writing as one of the major pitfalls in her content quality audit, specifically under the question of whether you got your audience right. Her remedy is practical: know your audience in terms of experience level, required jargon, task execution, and mental model, and involve people from that audience at every phase of the content design process rather than relying on your own expert framing.
